svg.title: Triangle constructions: compass estimate, ambiguous nonincluded angle, and angle-only scaling
svg.desc: First panel: two 5-centimeter segments join at one 40-degree angle; their endpoint-to-endpoint third side is about 3.42 centimeters, shorter than 5. Second panel: A to B is 8 centimeters, angle A measures 45 degrees, and a compass circle centered B with radius 6 centimeters intersects the positive 45-degree ray from A at two points, giving different third sides approximately 3.66 and 7.66 centimeters. Thus the same attached side-side-nonincluded-angle data admit two distinct noncongruent triangles. Third panel: two triangles, one twice the size of the other, have corresponding angles 50, 60, 70 degrees; three angle measures alone do not determine size. A 50, 60, 100 degree triple is impossible. Original Edulytiks coordinate models, not publisher artwork. Teacher reviews student drawings and measurements.
svg.text: Use a compass and protractor to find every possible triangle, not just one drawing
Third side ≈ 3.42 cm, shorter than 5 cm
BC=6 cm in both; AC ≈ 3.66 or 7.66
First-party reference only. Learner-created angle/compass models and explanations must be reviewed by a teacher.
